question: (i) Explain why Ampere’s circuital law becomes inconsistent when applied to the region between the plates of a charging capacitor. (ii) Hence obtain the expression for displacement current and show that it is equal to the conduction current in the connecting wires.

options.A:
(i) Ampere's law is consistent because the same current crosses every surface bounded by the loop.
(ii) $I_D=\varepsilon_0\Phi_E$ and it is unrelated to the current in the wires.
options.B:
(i) A surface through the wire encloses conduction current $I$, while a surface through the capacitor gap encloses no conduction current, giving different results for the same loop under the original law.
(ii) During charging, $\Phi_E=EA=\dfrac{q}{\varepsilon_0}$. Hence $I_D=\varepsilon_0\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}=\varepsilon_0\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(\dfrac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\right)=\dfrac{dq}{dt}=I$, equal to the conduction current.
options.C:
(i) The inconsistency occurs because a capacitor has too much conduction current between its plates.
(ii) $I_D=\dfrac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}=\dfrac{dq}{dt}$.
options.D:
(i) The original law fails only when the capacitor is uncharged.
(ii) $I_D=0$ in the gap because no charge crosses it.
